scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.

symptoms: Dispute ticket volume increase since August
problem_definition.root_problem: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced errors in bill calculation, causing the increase in dispute tickets since August.

trace.summary: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced errors in bill calculation, causing the increase in dispute tickets since August.

details.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

trace.summary: The structural fix (audit and revert of billing import validation rules) can be performed deterministically within the remaining time. LLM reasoning adds value to correlate specific rule changes with billing errors and to prioritize which rule to revert. Autonomous iteration is not needed because the remediation is a one‑time corrective action. After the rule fix, bills already issued with incorrect amounts require manual adjustments (K‑BILLWRITE) and cannot be automated, which is a residual exception. Monitoring dispute volume is needed to detect whether the fix restores the pre‑August baseline.

structural_remedies.description: Audit the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES), identify any rule changes made since July, revert to the prior rule set, and institute a change‑control review requiring Billing Operations approval before any future rule modification.
structural_remedies.rationale: Rule audit and rollback can be completed within the remaining 225 minutes; no automated bill writes are required, satisfying K-BILLWRITE.; residual gap: Bills already issued with incorrect amounts need manual adjustments; these require Billing Operations authority (K-BILLWRITE) and cannot be automated, so a manual re‑bill/credit process remains to be executed after the rule fix.
